candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and protect clients and healthcare personnel from environmental hazards.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — healthcare water-system infection prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the purpose of healthcare water-management programs: identify and control building-water conditions that permit Legionella and other pathogens to grow or spread, particularly in facilities serving vulnerable populations.

options.A: To identify and control conditions that permit Legionella and other waterborne pathogens to grow or spread, especially in complex systems serving vulnerable patients.
options.B: To eliminate the need for routine infection-prevention practices whenever tap water meets municipal drinking-water standards.
options.C: To replace all facility plumbing with sterile disposable tubing because building water systems cannot be managed safely.
options.D: To focus only on water taste and odor because healthcare-associated waterborne infections are not a recognized concern.

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends comprehensive water-management programs for healthcare facilities to reduce Legionella growth and transmission and to help control other waterborne pathogens. Healthcare facilities often have complex water systems and serve patients at increased risk for severe Legionnaires' disease. WMPs identify hazardous conditions, establish and monitor control measures, define corrective actions, and require ongoing verification/validation. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare water-management programs are used to identify and control conditions that allow Legionella and other waterborne pathogens to grow or spread in building water systems, particularly in facilities serving vulnerable patients.
candidate.source_locator: Key Points and Recommendations for Healthcare Facilities: comprehensive WMPs reduce Legionella growth/transmission and can control other waterborne pathogens. About WMPs/Risk in Healthcare Settings: healthcare facilities serve high-risk populations and may have large complex water systems; WMPs identify hazardous conditions and outline control steps.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: Why do healthcare facilities use water-management programs for building water systems?
